sources.title: Is it me or not me? Modulation of perceptual-motor awareness and visuomotor performance by mindfulness meditation
Theta Neurofeedback Training Supports Motor Performance and Flow Experience
sources.authors: Eschmann KCJ, Riedel L, Mecklinger A.
sources.journal: Journal of cognitive enhancement : towards the integration of theory and practice

findings.finding: Mindfulness meditation practice is associated with slower body movements which lead to better motor performance.
findings.quote: Mindfulness meditation practice is associated with slower body movements which in turn may lead to an increase in monitoring of body states and optimized re-adjustment of movement trajectory, and consequently to better motor performance.

findings.finding: Mindfulness training can enhance flow experience, which is associated with automatic and effortless control during challenges.
findings.quote: Flow is defined as a cognitive state that is associated with a feeling of automatic and effortless control, enabling peak performance in highly challenging situations. In sports, flow can be enhanced by mindfulness training

findings.finding: Mindfulness-based interventions can improve executive function and motor skill performance.
findings.quote: Preliminary evidence of efficacy was explored, primarily focusing on perceived stress and executive function and secondarily on burnout, depression, motor skill performance

principle: Mindfulness practice supports motor performance and flow by encouraging slower, more deliberate movements that enhance body awareness and trajectory control.
for_the_teacher: Encourage learners to perform movements more slowly at first to increase body state monitoring and trajectory control.
